hero.heading: Shred A Billion Roblox Wiki: Official Game Link and Starter Guides
hero.lead: Play [Shred A Billion on Roblox](https://www.roblox.com/games/125332227026284), the bank-vault experience by Blue Chip studios. Start with one trip from the bills to the shredder so you can see how you earn your first coins. If you already know the basics, jump to the sections on vacuum upgrades, the golden key, or the cart ride to the hideout.

sections.heading: Official Roblox Link: Look for Blue Chip studios
sections.intro: Open the [official Shred A Billion listing](https://www.roblox.com/games/125332227026284) to play. The experience ID is `125332227026284`, the number immediately after `/games/` in the Roblox address. The creator credit on the experience page reads Blue Chip studios.
paragraphs: If a search result or a shared link takes you to a Roblox page with a similar title, compare the experience ID before you press Play. You don't have to match every word in the address: a link can include the game name after the number. The important checks are the Roblox domain, the experience ID, and the creator credit on the destination page.
For a group outing, send the direct listing in your chat before everyone opens the game. That gives all of you the same page to start from and avoids having each person pick a result by title.

sections.heading: Start With the Hand Vac and Shred Bills for Coins
sections.intro: Your first job in the bank vault is to pick up bills with the starter hand vac. The bills you collect are not coins yet. Bring the cash to the shredder: each bundle you feed into it earns coins, which you can put toward better vacuums. That distinction matters if you've picked up plenty of bills but still haven't earned what you need for an upgrade.
paragraphs: For your first trip, take a small batch to the shredder instead of trying to clear every bill you see. A short trip gives you a chance to find your way from collection to shredding while your goal is still simple. A useful first milestone is seeing a batch through to coins, even if those coins aren't enough for the tool you want.

On a second trip, make the return part of your plan before you collect more. If you spent most of the first outing figuring out where to take the bills, repeat a route you recognize rather than extending the outing in a new direction. Once you're comfortable doing both parts, use the [beginner guide](/beginner-guide) if you need help deciding what to try next.
bullets: Take the hand vac into the bank vault and pick up bills.
Bring the cash bundles to the shredder to turn them into coins.
Put the coins toward a better vacuum, or make another trip if you need more.

sections.heading: Monsters Come Out at Night
sections.intro: Night brings monsters, so a collection goal that makes sense earlier in the outing may not be worth extending as it gets late. If you're still learning where to go, pick a stopping point you can recognize without estimating how much more cash is nearby. Finishing the trip you started is a different decision from heading out for another one.
paragraphs: For example, say you're deciding whether to follow more bills farther in or head back after reaching your original goal. If you're still getting your bearings, heading back is the simpler choice. If you choose to go farther, make that a deliberate decision to spend more of the outing collecting, especially when night is approaching.

The same idea applies when your goal is to explore rather than earn coins. Pick one thing you want to learn, such as where the path you're following leads, instead of treating every outing as a push to get as far as possible. That gives you a clear point at which to decide whether to keep going.

sections.heading: Which Vacuum Should You Work Toward?
sections.intro: The starting tool is a hand vac. The game also names backpack vacs, the Mega Vac, and the Black Hole as tools you can work toward. Use those names to recognize the equipment you're looking at. The names alone don't tell you how much to save or whether a particular purchase is right for the next thing you want to do.
paragraphs: If you're deciding whether to spend or save, start with the upgrade you can actually see in the game. Compare its displayed cost with the coins you have and read what it offers before deciding. For a first upgrade, it helps to choose a specific next purchase instead of saving indefinitely for the most recognizable name on the list.

Use the [vacuum guide](/tool) when your question is about the equipment itself, and the [upgrade guide](/upgrade) when you're deciding what to work toward next. Keep the equipment decision separate from the goal of getting the gold vault open: a vacuum is the tool you collect with, while the gold vault has its own requirement.

sections.heading: From Digging to the Gold Vault
sections.intro: The golden key is found by digging deeper, and it's what opens the gold vault. The vault you visit for bills and the gold vault serve different purposes. You don't need to find the key to get started with bills, and opening the gold vault is a milestone of its own rather than another name for earning a vacuum upgrade.
paragraphs: When you switch from earning coins to looking for the key, change what counts as progress. On a coin outing, you can judge your progress by what you bring back to the shredder. On a search outing, pay attention to where you've already dug and where you want to continue. Giving yourself one objective makes it easier to decide whether to keep digging or go back to earning coins.
Finding the key gets you to the next stage, not the end of the heist. Plan for another task after opening the gold vault: getting the gold onto carts for the trip out.

sections.heading: Get the Gold to the Hideout
sections.intro: Once the gold vault opens, the job changes from finding a way in to getting the gold out. Load the gold onto the carts, then ride out to the hideout. Think of opening the vault, loading the gold, and making the ride as separate milestones. That way, if you stop partway through, you can tell which part you still need to learn on your next attempt.
paragraphs: For a first heist, aim to finish the trip before worrying about how fast it looks. Pay attention to the transition after the vault opens: finding gold and getting it onto the carts are different steps. If you're playing with friends, it's also a good moment to make sure everyone knows the destination before you get busy with the carts.

If the trip feels confusing, focus on the next action in the sequence rather than trying to remember the whole run at once. After the vault is open, think about loading; after loading, think about the ride. Save the comparison with other runs for when you've seen where the trip ends.

sections.heading: Use the Leaderboard After a Complete Heist
sections.intro: The leaderboard ranks the fastest heists. It gives you something to compare once you've made a run, but it won't tell you what to practice by itself. On your first finish, pick the part that caused the most hesitation. Maybe you knew what to do with the gold but paused around the carts, or maybe the whole sequence was new. Those are different things to work on.
paragraphs: For a repeat attempt, change one thing you can judge for yourself. For instance, agree before the run that everyone should know the next step when you reach the carts, then see whether your group has fewer pauses there. That gives you a useful comparison even if your run doesn't put you near the top of the board.

When you share a result with friends, distinguish a personal best from a leaderboard position. A quicker run than your own last attempt is progress even when the fastest listed runs are still well ahead.

sections.heading: Pick One Goal Before Playing With Friends
sections.intro: A good first group session starts with an agreement about what everyone wants out of it. If some people are brand new, teach the starter trip before asking them to keep up on a gold run. If everyone knows the basics, agree on whether you're exploring for the key, trying to finish a heist, or attempting to beat a previous time.
paragraphs: Give that goal a clear endpoint. For a learning session, you might call it after everyone has tried their first trip. For a heist session, you might make reaching the hideout the goal and leave the time comparison for later. If you change objectives halfway through, say so; otherwise one person can be ready to move on while another is still trying to finish the original task.
Use the [co-op guide](/co-op) when you're setting up a session with friends and want help choosing what to do together.

faq.question: Who made Shred A Billion on Roblox?
faq.answer: Blue Chip studios is the creator credited on Roblox. On a shared link, read the byline on the experience page itself; the text somebody puts in a message or search result is not the creator credit.

faq.question: Can I play with friends in Shred A Billion?
faq.answer: You can bring up to three friends, which makes four players including you. When you're organizing a session, count yourself as one of the four rather than treating the advertised number of friends as the total group size.

faq.question: Is the advertised group reward a redeemable code?
faq.answer: The Roblox description offers 100 coins for joining the group. It describes a membership offer, not a code to type in. For that particular bonus, look for the group associated with the official experience instead of searching for a redemption phrase.
